name: Money navigation after the 2026-08 consolidation
purpose: Four tabbed portals hold all money screens: Customer Money (/admin/invoicing), Books and Tax (/admin/finances), Receipts and Cards (/admin/receipts) and the software subscription (/admin/billing). /admin/money is only a landing page.

elements.name: /admin/money landing
elements.does: Renders WorkspaceLanding for the 'money' workspace; no data of its own.

elements.name: Redirect stubs
elements.does: receivables, payments/inbox, invoicing/categories, finances/overview, finances/reconcile, reports, cards, pass-through, billing/invoices and billing/plan-history each redirect to a tab of one of the four portals.

behaviours: Tabs are driven by usePortalTabs with per-tab role lists; the collections tab is deliberately admin/developer only while its siblings also admit tech_support.
If a company switches every tab off the portal shows a 'switched off' message pointing to Settings, Pages.
problems: Consolidation is done but the vocabulary is still split: 'Billing' (software subscription) and 'Invoicing' (customers) are two portals about invoices, and Finances 'Job profitability' sits beside Reports.
Several comments and plan docs still name the old routes (/admin/money bank reconciliation, /admin/cards), so the plans no longer match the screens.
rebuild: One Money workspace with five top-level tabs: Sales (proposals, change orders, invoices, collections, incoming payments), Expenses (receipts, cards, mileage, pass-through), Payroll and payouts, Books (overview, reconcile, tax, reports), Plan and billing (software subscription, moved to Settings).
add: A single 'what needs me today' inbox: unmatched payments, stale claims, receipts to approve, bank rows to match
nationwide: Role names and portal labels are generic. The software subscription portal is the SaaS operator's concern and should not appear inside a firm's money area.

name: Invoices tab (customer invoice list)
purpose: Lists every customer invoice as a card with status, total, dates, linked job and a copy-pay-link button.

elements.name: New invoice
elements.does: Link to /admin/invoices/new.

elements.name: Payments inbox
elements.does: Link to the Incoming tab (via the old route).

elements.name: Invoice card
elements.does: Shows total, created/sent/due/paid dates, job badge linking to the job, mailto link, copy direct pay link.

behaviours: Non-paid invoices sort above paid ones, each group newest first.
API returns at most 200 rows, ordered by created_at, with no org filter and no search or pagination.
problems: Hard 200-row limit with no paging, search, date or customer filter: a busy firm loses older invoices from view.
Card grid is slow to scan for 'who has not paid'; that is what the Collections tab does, so the same data is shown two ways.
No edit, void, resend, record-payment or delete control on the card; resend and void exist only as API behaviour.
Admin list route filters only by role, not by org (service-role client, no org_id predicate).
rebuild: A dense table (number, customer, job, issued, due, total, balance, status) with filters, search, bulk send and a row drawer holding resend, void, record payment, credit and PDF.
add: Invoice PDF download for office use
Progress or milestone billing against a proposal
nationwide: Query is global across orgs. org_id column defaults to the Starr org UUID in seed 323. Must be scoped by active org.

name: New invoice composer
purpose: Type a customer and line items, optionally link a job, set a required upfront deposit, then create and email an invoice with a pay link.

elements.name: Linked job typeahead
elements.does: Searches /api/admin/jobs and stores job_id.

elements.name: Customer section
elements.does: Name, email, phone, billing address, plus 'use existing contact' prefill.

elements.name: Line items
elements.does: Description, quantity, unit price; add and remove rows; total computed client-side and server-side.

elements.name: Tax field
elements.does: A single dollar amount typed by hand; added to the total.

elements.name: Required upfront payment
elements.does: none, percent or fixed; resolved to deposit_amount_cents at create time.

elements.name: Create + send
elements.does: POST /api/admin/invoices (draft) then POST /api/admin/invoices/[id]/send (issued, email via Resend); shows the direct pay link after.

behaviours: Invoice number and a public slug are minted server-side; the slug is the customer's only credential.
Send route re-sends if already issued, refuses voided invoices, and in dev without RESEND_API_KEY still flips status.
A line-item picker from a service catalogue does not exist; the invoice categories tab is not wired into it.
problems: Invoices cannot be created from an accepted proposal or a priced job: everything is retyped.
Tax is one free-text dollar amount: no rate, taxable flag per line, jurisdiction or exemption.
No terms (net 30), no PO number, no discount, no attachments (plat, survey PDF).
Placeholder 'Thanks for choosing Starr Surveying!' is hard-coded.
889 lines in one component; no draft autosave.
rebuild: Build invoices from the proposal or job: line items come from the accepted quote and change orders, deposit and milestones are schedule rows, tax is computed from the job location by rule, and Send is one button with a preview of the email and PDF.
add: Create from proposal / job / change orders
Per-line taxability and a tax-rate engine
nationwide: Tax typed by hand; thank-you text hard-coded to Starr; USD only.

name: Collections tab (receivables aging)
purpose: Who owes money, how much and how late, in aging buckets.

elements.name: Outstanding and Past due totals
elements.does: Summary tiles.

elements.name: Bucket filter buttons
elements.does: Filter the table by age bucket.

elements.name: Table
elements.does: Invoice, customer, due, balance, age.

behaviours: Read-only; no reminder, call log or note is written from the page.
problems: Read-only: no 'send reminder', no promise-to-pay date, no notes, no escalation.
Still titled 'Receivables' (h1) inside a portal whose tab is 'Collections'.
Narrower role list than the portal, so tech_support sees three tabs not four, kept on purpose.
rebuild: Make aging a filter and a summary strip on the invoice list, with an automatic reminder schedule (day 1, 15, 30) and a per-invoice activity log.
nationwide: No state-specific rules (interest caps, lien deadlines). Mechanics lien and preliminary notice deadlines vary by state and matter for surveyors billing contractors.

name: Incoming tab (payments inbox and older claims)
purpose: Close-out queue for customer-claimed payments (Venmo, Cash App, Zelle) and pledged cash or checks that the office must confirm.

elements.name: Claim card
elements.does: Method, customer, email, submitted time, note, linked invoice (or 'Unlinked attempt').

elements.name: Mark cleared
elements.does: Optional transaction id or check number, then POST clear: writes a payments row, updates attempt and invoice status, sends the receipt email.

elements.name: Older claims
elements.does: Claims unconfirmed for 5 days or more, shown under the queue.

behaviours: Clear returns 409 if the attempt is already cleared, guarding double clicks.
Clearing is manual: nothing compares the claim to a bank row automatically.
problems: Confirmation is by memory and eyeball against the Venmo or bank history, not matched to the bank import.
No 'reject' or 'not received' action to close a false claim; the older-claims list can only grow.
Customer can claim 'I sent it' with no proof; any customer can queue a false claim against an invoice slug.
Partial payments handled by amount field only; no allocation across several invoices.
rebuild: One bank-driven 'Money in' queue: every deposit (Stripe payout, check, ACH, Venmo) is matched to an invoice, and a customer claim is only a hint that boosts the match.
add: Apply one payment to several invoices
Deposit slips for checks and mobile check deposit
nationwide: Venmo, Cash App and Zelle claims are consumer rails: many firms need ACH, wire, check and lockbox; none of these are handled with bank feeds.

name: Categories tab (allocation buckets)
purpose: Set target percentages for 18 seeded spending buckets (equipment, salaries, savings and so on) that a cleared payment is meant to be split into.

elements.name: Percent inputs per bucket
elements.does: Validated inline; save is disabled until active buckets sum to 100.

elements.name: Save
elements.does: PATCH categories.

behaviours: The tab describes itself as 'the line items invoices are built from' but it edits allocation percentages, not invoice line items.
allocatePayment is imported only by allocation-reports and category-editor; no payment path (Stripe webhook, clear route) calls it.
problems: Dead end: percentages are saved but nothing allocates payments with them.
The hint text says 'line items invoices are built from', which is wrong and confusing.
No add, delete or rename of a bucket.
rebuild: Delete from the invoicing portal. If the owner wants 'profit first' style envelopes, build it later as a Books report fed by the ledger. A real service catalogue (name, default price, GL account, taxable) belongs in the invoice composer.
add: Service catalogue with GL account mapping
nationwide: Bucket list is the Starr owner's personal allocation scheme.

name: Customer pay portal (/pay and /pay/[invoice])
purpose: A customer looks up an invoice by number and pays it by card or bank, by Venmo, Cash App or Zelle deep link, or pledges cash or a check.

elements.name: Lookup (/pay)
elements.does: Invoice number entry; firm name via usePublicFirm.

elements.name: Password gate
elements.does: PAY_PORTAL_PASSWORD env var; if unset the gate is open.

elements.name: Invoice page
elements.does: Line items, tax, deposit requirement, method picker, Stripe Elements card form, 'I sent it' and 'I will pay by cash or check' forms, receipt email button.

behaviours: Stripe PaymentIntent is created via the intent route; it returns 503 while PAYMENTS_LIVE is not 'true', so today a customer can see the invoice but not pay by card.
Public routes are rate-limited (B1-1).
The invoice number or slug is the only authorisation.
problems: Not live: PAYMENTS_LIVE gate and the pending owner checklist (publishable key, handle verification) are unfinished per the pending plan.
Wrong Venmo or Zelle handle gives no error and the money goes elsewhere; no verification is possible.
Brand colours in the card form are hard-coded to Starr navy and red.
No pay-by-text link, saved card, autopay or payment plan; no partial-payment amount picker beyond the deposit rule.
Emoji glyphs stand in for method logos.
rebuild: Branded per-firm hosted invoice page: one primary Pay button (card or ACH via Stripe), a quiet 'other ways to pay' section driven by the firm's own configured methods, and a receipt that links to the job portal.
add: ACH with micro-deposit or Financial Connections as the default for large invoices
nationwide: Handles and brand are Starr's; USD-only (non-USD intents are skipped); password gate is a launch placeholder; firm identity comes from the tenant profile only for emails.

name: Payment methods table and live switch
purpose: Defines the seven customer payment methods, gates every money-moving route on PAYMENTS_LIVE and reports whether Stripe keys are live or test.

elements.name: PAYMENT_METHODS
elements.does: Stripe, Venmo, Cash App, Zelle, ACH id, cash and check with labels, deep-link templates and handles.

elements.name: Readiness panel
elements.does: Shows blockers (test key, mixed pair, key in wrong variable, no company card); renders nothing when all is clear.

behaviours: Handles and the Venmo deep link recipient are string constants in a file imported by client components.
Plan notes making them configurable was investigated and deferred to an org_settings payments section.
problems: Single-tenant constants: another firm cannot set its own handles without a code change.
'ach' is in the method id type but there is no separate ACH handler; ACH is only a Stripe bank-account option.
Readiness panel is mounted on the Cards tab, an odd place to find 'is payments live?'.
rebuild: A per-org 'Get paid' settings page: connect Stripe (Connect/Standard), choose which methods to show, enter handles, with live test-payment and verification built in.
add: Test-mode toggle visible to the firm
nationwide: Hard-coded @StarrSurveying, $StarrSurveying and info@starr-surveying.com. Must live in org settings.

name: Stripe intent and webhook (customer payments)
purpose: Create a PaymentIntent for an invoice and, when Stripe confirms success, record the payment and update the invoice.

elements.name: Intent route
elements.does: Computes the amount (deposit first, never over balance), creates a PaymentIntent for card and us_bank_account, stores a shadow payment_intents row.

elements.name: Webhook
elements.does: Signature check, processed_webhook_events dedupe, then handlers for payment_intent.succeeded, payment_failed, checkout.session.completed and the subscription and invoice events of the software subscription.

behaviours: On success inserts a payments row, sets invoice status paid or partial and paid_at, and marks the shadow row succeeded; deduped on payments.external_id.
Non-USD intents are skipped; with PAYMENTS_LIVE false the event is logged and dropped.
The webhook does not email a receipt, does not allocate the payment, and does not handle refunds or disputes.
problems: No charge.refunded, charge.dispute.created, payment_intent.payment_failed for invoices, or ACH return handling: a returned ACH payment would stay recorded as paid.
Customer receipt is not sent by the webhook; only the office clear route and a manual 'email me a receipt' button send one.
Payments dropped when PAYMENTS_LIVE is false are not replayed.
Stripe fees and payouts are not recorded, so a Stripe deposit cannot be reconciled to a bank row.
One webhook endpoint serves invoice payments, wallet top-ups and software subscriptions.
rebuild: Separate endpoints for firm payments (Stripe Connect events) and the operator's own subscription. Store charge, fee, net and payout id; handle refund, dispute and ACH-return events; send the receipt from one place.
add: Fee and payout capture for reconciliation
nationwide: Uses one platform Stripe key; each firm needs its own connected account so funds do not pass through the operator.

name: Customer payment claims and receipts API
purpose: Records a customer's 'I sent it' claim or cash or check pledge and re-sends a receipt email with a PDF.

elements.name: attempt
elements.does: Creates payment_attempts in pending_confirmation (venmo, cashapp, zelle) or pledged (cash, check); enforces the upfront rule; refuses paid invoices.

elements.name: receipt
elements.does: Emails any address the visitor types a receipt for an invoice with cleared payments; logs payment_receipts.

behaviours: Intentionally not gated by PAYMENTS_LIVE.
Receipt PDF letterhead is drawn as 'STARR SURVEYING'.
problems: Receipt can be sent to any email by anyone who knows the number; fine but a spam and privacy vector.
PDF letterhead is hard-coded Starr text in receipt-pdf.ts.
No claim expiry or cancel.
rebuild: Keep, but take firm name, logo and address from the tenant profile in PDF and email; add claim cancellation and expiry.
add: Branded PDF receipts and invoices from the firm's logo
nationwide: STARR SURVEYING literal in PDF; firm identity helper exists (firmForOrg) but PDF does not use it everywhere.

name: Public proposal page and acceptance
purpose: A customer reads a priced proposal and accepts it by typing their name (optionally a drawn signature).

elements.name: Proposal view
elements.does: Scope of work, line items, terms, validity and view state (acceptable, expired, superseded, declined, accepted).

elements.name: Accept
elements.does: Typed name required; writes quote_acceptances (evidence), creates the job, marks lead won and quote accepted.

behaviours: Token is 256 bits from a CSPRNG; the IP is stored hashed.
A second accept returns success, not an error, because of a unique index.
problems: Acceptance creates a job but not an invoice or a deposit request, so the 'quote to invoice' hand-off stops at the job.
No customer-facing option to pay a retainer at acceptance.
Typed name is a weak signature; no email verification of the signer.
No admin UI composes or sends proposals (see money.proposal-admin-api), so this page can only be reached from API calls and tests.
rebuild: On acceptance create the job, the deposit invoice and the milestone schedule in one step, and take payment on the same page.
add: E-signature compliant with ESIGN and UETA
Optional line items the customer selects
nationwide: Texas assumptions are not hard-coded here; survey types and terms come from templates. Contract terms and licence statements are state-specific and must be per-firm templates.

name: Admin proposals, change orders, portal links and cost recoveries APIs
purpose: Back-end for composing proposals as append-only versions, raising change orders, issuing customer portal links and recording pass-through costs.

elements.name: proposals
elements.does: GET a lead's versions; POST creates the next version (supersedes the prior and nulls its token); PATCH send or decline.

elements.name: change-orders
elements.does: GET/POST/PATCH send, approve, decline, void; amounts are signed.

elements.name: portal-access
elements.does: Issue and revoke job links; full token shown once.

behaviours: Revisions are never edits, preserving the original figure.
problems: No admin page calls proposals, change-orders or portal-access: only tests and the public pages reference them, so the quote and change-order half of the flow is unreachable from the product.
Change orders are not tied into the invoice composer or the job budget.
Only cost-recoveries has a screen (Rebilled tab).
rebuild: Build the missing front end: a Proposal builder on the lead and job pages, a change-order button on the job, and a Share portal button, all feeding the same invoice schedule.
nationwide: Templates table is per firm in principle; no per-state clause library.

name: Public change-order approval
purpose: A customer approves or declines a scope change with a typed name and timestamp.

elements.name: Change order summary
elements.does: Description, signed amount, days added, job and firm.

elements.name: Approve / Decline
elements.does: Records the decision once; a repeat click is treated as success.

behaviours: Same evidence rules as proposals.
problems: Approval does not add a line to an invoice or move a due date.
Cannot be reached unless something calls the admin API, which has no UI.
rebuild: Approval appends a line to the job's billing schedule and notifies the project manager.
nationwide: Generic; wording needs per-firm templates.

name: Customer job portal
purpose: A customer follows one job: phase, deliverables, invoices and change orders.

elements.name: Phase and deliverables
elements.does: Allow-listed projections of the job.

elements.name: Invoices list
elements.does: Invoice number, slug, total, status, dates, with pay links.

elements.name: Change orders
elements.does: List with links to approval.

behaviours: Every query selects named columns, never select('*'), as a disclosure rule.
Token grants one job.
problems: Depends on portal-access links that the office cannot yet issue from any screen.
Two different customer entry points exist: /pay by invoice number and /portal by token.
rebuild: One customer link per job, which holds proposal, invoices with Pay, change orders, deliverables and messages.
add: Pay all open invoices at once
nationwide: Firm name from tenant profile; otherwise generic.

name: Public services pricing page
purpose: Marketing page with price ranges for 11 survey types plus an embedded calculator.

elements.name: Service cards
elements.does: Title, range, turnaround, description; all labelled estimates.

elements.name: Calculator
elements.does: Dynamically imported estimator.

behaviours: Static arrays in the page; no database.
problems: Ranges are hard-coded in JSX, not tied to the firm's service catalogue or to proposal templates, so three places can disagree.
Ranges are Texas Central pricing and copy mentions Starr.
rebuild: Generate from the firm's service catalogue (the same one the proposal and invoice use), with a 'request a quote' form that creates a lead.
nationwide: Every price, turnaround and text is Starr's local market; per-firm and per-region data needed.

name: Software bundle pricing page
purpose: SaaS plan tiles (Recon, Draft, Field, Office, Academy, Firm Suite) with monthly and annual toggle and Start free trial to /signup.

elements.name: Bundle tiles
elements.does: Price and feature list per bundle.

elements.name: Monthly/annual toggle
elements.does: Switches the displayed price.

elements.name: Start free trial
elements.does: Links to /signup?bundle=id.

behaviours: Sold under the Starr Software brand, separate from the surveying firm.
problems: Stripe checkout for the subscription is not wired (customer portal returns 'being finalized'), so the page promises a purchase path that does not exist end to end.
rebuild: Keep as the operator's marketing page; connect to real Stripe Checkout and Billing portal.
nationwide: Operator-side page, not firm-side.

name: Billing (software subscription) portal
purpose: What the firm pays for the platform: current plan, subscription invoices and plan history.

elements.name: Overview tab
elements.does: Plan and subscription state.

elements.name: Invoices tab
elements.does: Stripe subscription invoices from the invoices table.

elements.name: Plan history tab
elements.does: Past plan changes.

elements.name: Cancel
elements.does: Sets cancel_at_period_end.

elements.name: Manage payment methods
elements.does: Stripe Customer Portal redirect; returns a 'being finalized' message when the customer id or key is missing.

behaviours: Reads the live `invoices` table (Stripe subscription schema), distinct from customer_invoices.
problems: Name collides with customer invoicing in the same Money menu; owners cannot tell 'my invoices' from 'invoices I send'.
847-line page and Stripe flow not finished (portal returns placeholder).

The payments-invoices collision doc is stale: customer invoices now live in customer_invoices and only billing and platform routes read invoices, yet the doc still says the pay feature is broken and awaiting a decision.
The webhook's subscription handlers write research_subscriptions; what populates the invoices table the Billing tab reads was not found in the webhook (status unknown).
rebuild: Move to Settings, Plan and billing, using the Stripe-hosted customer portal for everything: no custom invoices tab.
add: Tax ID and billing address on file
nationwide: Operator concern; per-firm plan data already org based.

name: Bundle upgrade prompt
purpose: Landing page for users who open a feature their bundle does not include.

elements.name: Upgrade CTA
elements.does: Links to /admin/billing.

elements.name: Contact support
elements.does: mailto:support@starrsoftware.com.

elements.name: Back link
elements.does: returnTo.

behaviours: Middleware gate that would send people here is described as gated on an auth refactor.
problems: Unclear whether anything redirects here; the support address is hard-coded.
rebuild: Fold into the billing settings page as a section.
nationwide: Operator page.

name: Finances Overview (money in vs money out)
purpose: Revenue, payouts, expenses and net for a date range with a per-period breakdown.

elements.name: Quick ranges
elements.does: This year, last year, 90 days, 30 days.

elements.name: Load / export
elements.does: Fetch and CSV.

behaviours: Cash-basis style rollup of payments in, payouts and approved receipts out.
problems: Not an accounting P&L: no accrual, no chart of accounts, no A/P.
Overlaps the Reports tab financials and the job profitability tab.
rebuild: One Books dashboard (cash and accrual toggle) backed by a ledger, with the other tabs becoming views of it.
add: Sync to QuickBooks or Xero in place of a built-in ledger
nationwide: Generic.

name: Job profitability tab (Schedule C report)
purpose: Tax-time summary joining approved receipts and mileage into Schedule C lines, with a period lock.

elements.name: Year picker, Refresh, Export CSV
elements.does: Loads and downloads the tax summary.

elements.name: Lock period
elements.does: mark-exported flags rows as exported to prevent double counting.

elements.name: Schedule C table, mileage, vendor and submitter tables
elements.does: Breakdowns for the preparer.

behaviours: Footnote says the CPA can re-classify in QuickBooks before filing.
problems: The tab is labelled 'Job profitability' with hint 'what each job cost and what it earned', but the component is the Schedule C tax report: the label and content do not match. Per-job margin lives at /admin/reports/job/[jobId].
Schedule C is for sole proprietors; an LLC or S-corp files 1120-S or 1065 and needs different mapping.
1008-line component.
rebuild: Rename to Tax export. Provide a category-to-GL mapping and export to QuickBooks or Xero or the CPA's tool, with entity-type specific forms.
add: Entity type setting (sole prop, LLC, S-corp, partnership)
nationwide: US federal sole-proprietor form only; state income and franchise taxes (e.g. Texas margin tax) are not covered.

name: Bank reconciliation (PNC CSV)
purpose: Import a bank CSV and match each row to a payout, expense or customer payment.

elements.name: CSV upload and Import
elements.does: Parses a PNC-format CSV and de-duplicates on a fingerprint.

elements.name: Suggested matches (up to 3)
elements.does: Scored by amount and date within 5 days; Confirm or Ignore.

behaviours: No Plaid or bank API by design.
Parser is named PNC and accepts that bank's column layout.
problems: PNC-only parser: other banks fail or mis-parse.
Matching targets are internal records only; there is no ledger posting and no 'unmatched, categorise' flow for fees, interest or owner draws.
Customer payments from Stripe arrive as net payouts that combine several invoices and fees; there is no match model for them.
Matched state does not feed the invoice status: an invoice is paid by clearing a claim, independent of the bank.
rebuild: Bank feed via Plaid or an accounting-package feed, rules-based categorisation, Stripe payout splitting by charge, and period close with a reconciled balance.
add: QuickBooks or Xero bank feed sync
nationwide: PNC format only; other firms bank elsewhere.

name: Payroll tax and 1099 report
purpose: Per-person payout totals by period split into W-2, 1099 and unclassified, flagging 1099-NEC reportables.

elements.name: Quick ranges
elements.does: Year, prior year, Q1 to Q4.

elements.name: Download CSV
elements.does: Same endpoint with format=csv.

elements.name: Classification summary
elements.does: Counts and totals by W-2, 1099, unclassified; 'needs 1099-NEC' flag at 600 dollars.

behaviours: Classification is set manually; the app says it does not make the legal determination.
data: worker classification on the employee record
problems: Only the 600 dollar NEC threshold; no TIN or W-9 collection, no 1099-NEC form or e-file, no 1099-K or 1099-MISC for vendors.
The threshold is a fixed 600 dollar constant, not year-aware; federal law changed it to 2,000 dollars for payments made from 2026 (verify with the CPA), so this report likely over-flags.
Hint text says 'what was withheld and what is owed' but this is a payout report: no withholding, no Form 941 or 940, no state unemployment.
Vendors paid from expenses are not included; 1099 reporting for subcontracted crews and vendors is missing.
rebuild: Do not build payroll tax in-house: integrate a payroll provider (Gusto, ADP, Check) and a 1099 e-file service, and keep this as a read-only view of what they report. Collect W-9 for every contractor and vendor at onboarding.
add: W-9 and TIN collection with encryption
State unemployment and workers comp reporting
nationwide: Federal thresholds only; state payroll law is mentioned only in the payout autopilot plan (Texas Payday Law).

826-line tab with five sections; the job report lacks revenue from customer_invoices unless verified (status unknown).
Overlaps overview financials.

add: Revenue by client and survey type
Work in progress under billed or over billed

elements.name: Filters
